title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone Off Alaska; Atka Mackerel in the Bering Sea Subarea and Eastern Aleutian District of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area
summary:
NOAA Fisheries has temporarily closed directed fishing for Atka mackerel in parts of the Bering Sea and the eastern Aleutian Islands for a segment of the trawl fleet, effective October 9 through the end of 2025. The agency says the fleet has reached its annual catch limit for this area and needs to stop targeting the species to prevent an overrun.

This decision benefits the long-term health of Atka mackerel and the broader ecosystem. By staying within the set limits, managers aim to keep the stock stable, support future fishing opportunities, and maintain balance for other species and ocean users. Communities that rely on sustainable fisheries and the businesses that plan around predictable rules also gain from keeping catches within bounds.

On the other hand, the closure will likely hit some harvesters, crew, and processors in the trawl sector who depend on Atka mackerel for late-season revenue. Coastal communities tied to these operations may feel the ripple effects through less work and reduced landings. Market supply for Atka mackerel could tighten in the short term, which may affect buyers and pricing. While boats can keep small incidental catches taken while fishing for other species, they can’t target Atka mackerel directly for the rest of the year in the affected areas.

NOAA acted quickly based on catch data received October 6, skipping advance notice to avoid exceeding the limit. It’s a short-notice change, but the goal is straightforward: protect the resource now so it remains available in the years ahead.
